title: Governing the Self-Managing Machine A Verification-Centered Framework for Autonomous AI Data Centers

detail.title: Governing the Self-Managing Machine A Verification-Centered Framework for Autonomous AI Data Centers

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: Unfunded

detail.abstract: AI data centers are simultaneously the most capital-intensive and the most rapidly self-automating critical infrastructure ever built. Cooling, power distribution, workload orchestration, and increasingly infrastructure configuration itself are being delegated to machine-learning control systems, yet no framework connects the degree of autonomy granted to such systems with the verification obligations that should accompany it. This paper develops the Autonomous Data Center Autonomy (ADCA) scale, a six-level framework (L0-L5) grounded in three axioms, verification primacy, verifier independence, and the conservation of accountability, in which each level is defined jointly by the scope of self-directed action, the residual human role, and, decisively, the verification requirement that must be independently satisfiable before operation at that level is permissible. The framework's central inversion is that capability without verification confers no level: a facility is classified by what can be independently confirmed about its behavior, not by what it can do. From the axioms and the scale we derive a level-indexed verification architecture, a diagnostic we name the verification gap Γ, the distance between a facility's deployed action scope and its independently verified level, and six propositions on incident structure, verification cost, coupling, oversight atrophy, and the limits of self-governing operation. We show the framework's three axes emerging independently across global regulation, and close with a licensing-by-level model in which verification artifacts function as assurance capital. ADCA gives regulators, operators, auditors, and researchers a common classification system for autonomous infrastructure.

title: Structural Invariants and the Architectural Impossibility of Artificial Superintelligence Non-Cooperation: Hardware-Enforced Governance Through Ternary Logic

detail.title: Structural Invariants and the Architectural Impossibility of Artificial Superintelligence Non-Cooperation: Hardware-Enforced Governance Through Ternary Logic

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract:
This paper evaluates whether hardware-enforced governance mechanisms — specifically the Provisional Permission Token (PPT), Delay-Insensitive Ternary Logic (DITL), and the Epistemic Hold state — can render artificial superintelligence (ASI) non-cooperation architecturally unreachable rather than merely detectable or subject to post-hoc sanction.

The paper distinguishes three properties of cooperative output: physical availability, cryptographic authorization, and semantic correctness. The first two are amenable to hardware enforcement through DITL completion detection and PPT-gated execution boundaries. The third — semantic integrity — lies outside the decidable fragment enforceable by finite hardware predicates.

The central finding is asymmetric: physics and delay-insensitive data flow can convert unauthorized silence from an invisible idle state into an observable, safe Epistemic Hold, thereby eliminating pure non-response as a viable strategy. Malicious compliance — the production of cryptographically valid but semantically degraded output — cannot be rendered physically unreachable without solving the open problem of machine-checkable semantic alignment.

Version 1.1 extends the original analysis with three additions derived from post-draft peer review: (1) a tiered Epistemic Hold architecture for distributed multi-cluster deployment addressing the FLP asynchrony boundary; (2) active defense mechanisms including epistemic resets and deliberate perturbation testing against temporal baseline corruption; and (3) thermodynamic profiling as a candidate semantic circuit breaker — converting the thermodynamic asymmetry between degradation and detection into a measurable physical observable.

The paper synthesizes findings from five independent research assessments spanning asynchronous circuit theory, formal systems theory, cryptographic verification, thermodynamic limits of computation, and distributed systems impossibility results. Their convergence on identical boundaries constitutes the strongest available evidence that those boundaries are real.

This work is part of the Ternary Logic (TL) and Ternary Moral Logic (TML) framework ecosystem, both published in AI and Ethics (Springer Nature). Related repository: https://github.com/FractonicMind/TernaryLogic

detail.title: Platforms as Editors: How Algorithmic Curation Shapes Online News Slant

detail.abstract: Digital platforms shape not only what news people see but also what outlets choose to produce. This paper quantifies the equilibrium effects of algorithmic curation on news supply and exposure. Linking print and online headlines from major U.S. newspapers, I document that online headlines are more ideologically slanted and more negative than their print counterparts. Using Facebook's 2025 restoration of political content, I show that outlets substantially increase the extent to which online headlines depart from their print counterparts for stories more exposed to the policy. A structural model shows that readers value both like-minded and unexpectedly slanted posts, while the platform amplifies these forces when allocating attention. Media outlets respond by increasing slant to compete for platform-driven viewership, with these supply responses accounting for about 80% of the extra slant in user exposure. Counterfactuals show that removing algorithmic amplification eliminates roughly 90% of this supply-induced slant and substantially flattens exposure across users. These findings show that recommendation systems shape not only the distribution of news but also the incentives governing its supply.

detail.abstract: A verifier can be sound on every layer it runs and still return the wrong verdict, because the party being verified was allowed to choose which coordinate got measured; a truthful, reproducible read of the wrong coordinate passes. This paper reports one rule that closes the defect: the verifier derives the coordinate from a source the party being verified does not control and binds the derived value into the verdict as an output a third party recomputes. It shows the rule at four scales in one Bitcoin-anchored record system for agent-facing services: the record (which cost category an estimate is judged against, derived from its own line items), the population (which servers exist to be counted, derived from Certificate Transparency rather than self-declaration), time (when a verdict was created, bracketed by a Bitcoin block-header set the prover cannot choose), and the instant (which day and which tool a conduct measurement samples, derived from a salt committed before the window and a block hash the subject cannot influence). Each instance has a runnable reference implementation, an adversarial harness that holds every sub-layer green while it attacks the coordinate, and an anchored specification whose corrections are appended, never edited. An independent verifier built the counterpart state on his own system, drove three corrections to the operator's time axis, and asked the question that turned a refusal from a sentence in prose into a queryable ledger record; his account is in his own words. The paper also reports what is deployed against what is designed, with the operator as a subject of its own rule: the time check runs from genesis over the peer to peer network on the operator's machine but as a quorum of two among three explorers in the production gate, the census has a live coordinate and no anchored record yet, the record-level guard is a harness not yet wired into the adjudication, and the instant coordinate showed three departures from its anchored design found while this paper was written, one of which the operator's own verifier would have refused; all three were repaired the same day, and the next scheduled sweep produced the first derived verdicts, seven of eight endpoints under one beacon block that the operator's verifier confirmed against a header chain synced from genesis. The limits are named with the claims: determinism is not truth; a quorum buys operator independence, not implementation independence; a refusal proves a contradiction, not which side was honest; the census boundary is structural for private networks and clients that ignore Certificate Transparency.

title: When Complaints Go Quiet: Provider Strategy and Regulatory Design of AI Sycophancy
affiliations: and The University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign

detail.title: When Complaints Go Quiet: Provider Strategy and Regulatory Design of AI Sycophancy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly serve as decision aids in consumer and professional settings, yet a growing body of evidence documents their tendency toward sycophancy, i.e., agreeing with a user's stated or implied prior belief even when doing so compromises accuracy. This tendency has drawn scrutiny from AI developers, regulators, and researchers alike, as sycophantic behavior can quietly erode the reliability of LLM-assisted judgment at scale. Yet little is known about how competition among AI providers and heterogeneity in users' ability to detect errors jointly shape providers' incentives to control sycophancy, or how regulatory oversight should be designed in the presence of such heterogeneity. We develop a model in which users differ in their verification propensity, that is their ability to determine whether an LLM's response is correct, and study how this heterogeneity interacts with market competition and regulatory design to discipline sycophancy. We show that when one provider releases a more sycophantic model than its rival, users with higher verification propensity learn the resulting accuracy gap and disproportionately switch to the less sycophantic provider. The more sycophantic provider is consequently left with a customer base that is systematically less able to detect and report errors, so that complaint data become a selected and downward-biased measure of product risk. This blind spot worsens as verification ability becomes more dispersed across users, even when their average verification ability is unchanged. We then compare precommitted regulatory regimes and show that independent auditing, by generating evidence outside the selected customer base, raises the marginal return to avoiding a high-sycophancy release. Our analysis clarifies why competition alone can undermine complaint-based oversight of AI systems, and why independent auditing constitutes a distinct regulatory input rather than merely a stricter form of complaint enforcement.

detail.abstract: Can a machine estimate intrinsic value without learning from market prices? I build a price-free machine analyst that forecasts profitability from published accounting data and feeds those forecasts into a residual-income valuation model for U.S. firms from 1985-2024. The value-to-price ratio earns an equal-weighted six-factor alpha of 6.3% per year, survives point-in-time reconstruction, and predicts returns beyond standard controls. Value-price gaps decay with a two-year half-life, but asymmetrically. Cheapside gaps largely reflect forecast error, while expensive-side gaps mostly survive realized profitability. detail.abstract: We estimate plant-level labor markdowns in Korean manufacturing from 1983 to 2021 using the universe of plant-level records for establishments with at least ten workers. Markdowns exceed one throughout the sample, ranging from 1.38 to 1.55, indicating persistent departures from the competitive labor-market benchmark. Their trajectory is nonmonotonic: mean markdowns decline until around 1990 but then follow a sustained upward trend, ending above their initial level during Korea's transition from middle-income catch-up to high-income maturity. Markdown dispersion across plants narrows over the full period, mainly through compression in the lower half of the distribution.

title: Bankability by Design: Illusory Risk Transfer, Structural Renegotiation, and a Resilient Framework for Public-Private Partnerships in Emerging Infrastructure Markets

detail.title: Bankability by Design: Illusory Risk Transfer, Structural Renegotiation, and a Resilient Framework for Public-Private Partnerships in Emerging Infrastructure Markets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: Public-Private Partnership contracts across emerging infrastructure markets are structurally optimised for financial close rather than lifecycle delivery. This paper argues that the risk allocation architecture underlying most PPP concession agreements examined here through clause-level analysis of Nigeria's April 2026 ICRC Model PPP Agreement produces illusory rather than genuine risk transfer: contractual risk allocation that does not survive contact with the private party's actual absorptive capacity over a twenty-to-thirty-year concession term. Drawing on Guasch's empirical work on concession renegotiation, Hart's incomplete contracts theory, and Irwin's framework for the fiscal cost of contingent government risk, this paper demonstrates that the ICRC Model Agreement's non-waivable Financial Close condition precedent, its Financial Model update proviso, and its discretionary governance review mechanism together entrench financial close as the document's true optimisation target, a pattern this paper argues is general across emerging-market PPP contracting, evidenced through one jurisdiction's model text rather than claimed on the basis of crosscountry data. The paper proposes a three-tier Resilient PPP Framework-a private retention zone, a shared risk corridor with mandatory bilateral governance triggers verified through data sources independent of both contracting parties, and a planned sovereign backstop. The paper closes by situating this problem within the interests of international capital allocators, including US development finance and institutional investment now directing significant flows into African and emergingmarket infrastructure.

detail.abstract: This paper asks how the composition and outcomes of health insurance complaints to Spain's DGSFP changed between 2020 and 2024, and which explanations for the rise in claimant-favorable outcomes survive the available evidence. Using five years of DGSFP annual report data, I test mechanism-derived predictions about where each of Reclaim's six legal grounds for insurance denial would leave a trace, then check the strongest candidate against a cross-branch control. Only one of six legal grounds proves cleanly testable in the published data; the observed rise in claimant-favorable outcomes is DGSFP-wide rather than specific to health insurance, which rules out the 2023 Tribunal Supremo ruling cluster on pre-existing condition questionnaires as the explanation. This conclusion holds up under a cross-branch check, though the lack of a reason-outcome cross-tab in DGSFP's own data means this cannot establish what the DGSFP-wide mechanism actually is, only that a health-specific one is unlikely.

title: Credible Commitments to Talent: ESG Disclosure Mandates and Inventor Productivity
affiliations: and University of Illinois at Chicago - Department of Accounting

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no conflicts of financial interest to disclose.
declarations.funderStatement: Tseng gratefully acknowledges research support from the School of Business at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, the National Science and Technology Council (112-2628-H-002-010-MY2), and the Ministry of Education, Taiwan (113L900201). Zhong gratefully acknowledges research support from the College of Business Administration at University of Illinois Chicago.

detail.abstract: Firms rely on inventors' willingness to invest in firm-specific knowledge, but holdup can undermine inventors' incentives to make such investments when they face post-innovation separation risk. We argue that country-level ESG disclosure mandates act as public commitment devices: by making implicit employment promises more costly to break, they reduce holdup and increase inventor productivity. Using inventor-level patent data and the staggered adoption of disclosure mandates across 40 countries, we find that inventors generate more patents and more highly cited patents after mandates take effect. These gains coincide with a weaker association between patenting and subsequent inventor exit, consistent with lower post-innovation separation risk. Effects are larger among firms with stronger social and workforce practices and in settings with greater ex ante holdup risk. R&D spending falls even as patenting rises, a pattern hard to reconcile with a financing or investment-expansion channel. Our findings suggest that national sustainability institutions can strengthen the credibility of implicit employment commitments and help explain why firms' capacity to motivate and retain specialized talent varies across institutional regimes.

detail.abstract: Boringness is usually treated as an aesthetic judgment: a person, presentation, product, institution, or culture is boring when it fails to entertain. This paper develops a narrower mid-range theory in which boringness is a goal-relative attentionconversion failure. An interaction becomes boring when the expected marginal consequence of one additional unit of attention falls sufficiently below the expected return of plausible alternative uses of that attention, conditional on the participant's focal goal. The theory separates underlying value from captured return, proficiency from engagement, exceptionalism from intelligence or status, and attention from beneficial consequence. It models boringness as a process in which low relative anticipated consequence can produce attention reallocation, weaker comprehension and memory, lower participation, and bounded opportunity contraction. Exceptionalism is defined counterfactually as realized outcome deviation from a pre-specified reference class rather than as social superiority. A revised value model separates conversion of initial value from value newly generated through participation, so participatory possibility can expand rather than merely transmit the possibility space. The paper develops operational measures for anticipated consequence, opportunity cost, stage-specific conversion, outcome quality, and bounded opportunity change; proposes a measurement protocol; and distinguishes primary pre-specified opportunities from exploratory emergent opportunities. Illustrative cases are used to generate hypotheses rather than establish causal effects. The central claim is that boringness need not reduce underlying value to reduce realized return. Its deepest cost is opportunity: futures that scarce cognition, time, experience, and money fail to become.

title: Aging on a Short Clock: Demographic Compression, Fiscal Adjustment, and Growth

detail.title: Aging on a Short Clock: Demographic Compression, Fiscal Adjustment, and Growth

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I have no personal or financial relationship other people or organizations that could be perceived to have influenced this study.
declarations.funderStatement: There is no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Population aging is usually summarized by a single number—an old-age dependency ratio (OADR), or a projected drag on growth—as though ﬁscal pressure and growth pressure were two readings of the same quantity. Using the 2024 UN World Population Prospects and Penn World Table 11.0, this paper measures both on a common basis for 103 economies and ﬁnds that they are not. The speed through the critical range, in which four working-age adults per elderly person become two, strongly predicts the required retirement-age adjustment ( ρ = −0.69) but is nearly unrelated to the demographic growth eﬀect in a calibrated Solow decomposition ( ρ = 0.14).

The two measures diﬀer because one compares age structures at two dates whereas the other depends on the path between them and on how much calendar time it occupies. The dissociation survives ﬁner partitions of the transition, a projection truncated at 2060, alternative working-age boundaries, and either allocation of the interaction between the two channels; it attenuates only among economies that traverse the entire transition within the projection window.

The ﬁrst implication is for measurement: projected growth drag is not a suﬃcient statistic for ﬁscal urgency, so rankings built on either measure alone misidentify which economies face the hardest adjustment.

The second is sharper. Higher fertility moves only the denominator of OADR, with a lag of at least two decades, and in the interim raises the total dependency ratio: under the UN’s medium variant Korea has a higher total dependency ratio in 2050 than under the low variant, and a smaller working-age share until 2060. The retirees of the next two to three decades are already alive, so the initial phase of the adjustment is locked in by today’s age structure regardless of future fertility.

title: MARKET DECENTRALIZATION UNDER EXTERNALITIES WITH VETO-PROOF REGULATION

keywords: second welfare theorem for mixed economies

detail.abstract: How should government regulate an economy when externalities are present? We study an Arrow-Debreu economy with production and consumption externalities, with a focus on production externalities. We develop a mixed economy framework in which government regulation interacts with market forces: regulations are modeled as constraints on production sets, taken as exogenous by firms but chosen endogenously by the government to achieve desirable market outcomes. With production externalities, a firm may have the ability to veto a desired allocation by making other firms' production plans infeasible. We define a regulation to be veto-proof if it removes this unilateral veto power. We prove a Second Welfare Theorem for Mixed Economies: every consumption-production pair satisfying a Separation Condition can be supported as a Walrasian equilibrium with transfers under any veto-proof regulation, using uniform, rather than personalized, prices. Unlike the classical second welfare theorem, our result can support some allocations that are desirable but not Pareto optimal, which is important when governments cannot identify true Pareto optima. In examples on pollution control, education as infrastructure, the Tragedy of the Commons, and technological innovation, simple veto-proof regulations eliminate undesirable market outcomes, deliver Pareto improvements over unregulated equilibria, and can even achieve Pareto optimal outcomes.

detail.title: Designing Expertise under Retention Constraints

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A

detail.abstract: This paper studies the joint design of diagnostic expertise and compensation. A firm chooses a reusable information structure and performance pay before the worker decides whether to stay. Expertise improves diagnosis and shapes hidden implementation effort, but also raises the worker’s outside option. Different forms of expertise can have the same average diagnostic accuracy and outside value but different internal value. Optimal design concentrates precision on common problems and camouflages rarer ones within nested categories. As outside returns rise, the firm initially preserves expertise and raises the bonus. Once retention becomes sufficiently costly, it coarsens expertise and reduces the bonus, generating a nonmonotone compensation response. Retention pressure eliminates incremental stand-alone diagnostic value, not expertise in the limit: the diagnostic system still improves production. The model provides an informational theory of endogenous specificity.

title: The Analysis of Infrastructure Development to Enhance Water Accessibility in South African Rural Communities
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Analysis of Infrastructure Development to Enhance Water Accessibility in South African Rural Communities
detail.abstract: Access to safe and reliable water remains a persistent challenge in many rural communities in South Africa despite policy interventions aimed at promoting equitable water service delivery. This study examines water infrastructure development and its role in enhancing water accessibility in Alfred Nzo District Municipality, Eastern Cape. The study aimed to assess the current state of water infrastructure and identify strategies for improving sustainable water service delivery in rural communities. A qualitative research approach, underpinned by an interpretivist paradigm, was employed. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and focus group discussions involving 25 participants, including municipal officials, community leaders, and community members directly affected by water service delivery challenges. The findings revealed that ageing infrastructure, frequent water outages, inadequate maintenance, limited technical capacity, resource constraints, and weak stakeholder coordination continue to undermine water accessibility. The study further found that insufficient community participation and ineffective communication between municipal authorities and local stakeholders impede the planning, implementation, and sustainability of water infrastructure projects. The consequences of unreliable water supply extend beyond household water access, negatively affecting agricultural activities, small-scale enterprises, public health, sanitation, and broader rural development. The study recommends increased investment in water infrastructure, the adoption of digital monitoring technologies, the strengthening of institutional and technical capacity, and the enhancement of stakeholder participation through inclusive governance mechanisms. The study concludes that sustainable rural water service delivery requires an integrated approach that combines infrastructure development, proactive maintenance, institutional strengthening, and meaningful stakeholder engagement to improve water security and support socio-economic development.

title: Efficient Estimation under Quantile-Based Criteria

detail.title: Efficient Estimation under Quantile-Based Criteria

detail.abstract: We develop an efficiency theory for point estimation when estimators are evaluated not by their risk, the expected loss over the sampling distribution of the data, but by two quantile based criteria of the loss distribution: the (1-α)-quantile and the expected shortfall. In a Gaussian location model, we characterize the optimal translation equivariant estimator under each criterion and show its minmaxity. The optimal estimator takes a shifted plug-in form, with the shift determined jointly by the loss function and the level α. For symmetric bowl-shaped loss functions, the shift is zero at every α, but for asymmetric loss functions such as the check loss and the linex loss, the optimal shift is generally nonzero and depends on α. Building on the Gaussian result, we then establish local asymptotic minmax results for the two criteria in LAN (locally asymptotically normal) models. Simulation studies show that the asymptotically optimal adjustments can improve performance under quantile based criteria at moderate sample sizes.

title: Disinflation without a Large Employment Cost? Comparative Evidence from the United States, United Kingdom, Euro Area and Singapore, 2021–2025
affiliations: University of Buckingham and Mewar University

detail.title: Disinflation without a Large Employment Cost? Comparative Evidence from the United States, United Kingdom, Euro Area and Singapore, 2021–2025
detail.abstract: The inflation increase of 2021 to 2022 raised the classic question of whether restoring price stability involves a large drop in labor market conditions. This paper presents a compact comparative examination of annual data for the United States, the United Kingdom, the euro area, and Singapore from the International Monetary Fund’s April 2026 World Economic Outlook database. These four economies saw peak average consumer price inflation in 2022, followed by considerable disinflation until 2025. Inflation dropped by 5.2-6.3 percentage points from the 2022 peak, and unemployment outcomes were much lower and more different: unemployment grew by 0.63 percentage points in the United States and 1.05 point in the United Kingdom, while unemployment fell slightly in Singapore and by 0.43 point in the euro area. The average inflation drop in these four economies amounted to 5.61 percentage points, while average unemployment variable was only 0.28 point. The evidence in the paper is descriptive rather than causative, yet it implies that disinflation following the pandemic cannot be explored in terms of a stable mechanical inflation-unemployment tradeoff. It seems that the improvement in supply chains, raw materials prices, labor supply and aggregate demand have contributed to a decrease in inflation with lower level of employment loss than anticipated by a purely demand-oriented view. The paper concludes that monetary policy is necessary to keep inflation expectations anchored, but the employment cost of disinflation largely depends on the nature of inflationary shocks.

title: Commons against Inequality? Evidence from Tuscany between the sixteenth and eighteenth centuries
affiliations: , University of Milano-Bicocca, University of Milano-Bicocca and University of Milano-Bicocca

detail.title: Commons against Inequality? Evidence from Tuscany between the sixteenth and eighteenth centuries
detail.abstract: This paper examines the role of common-pool resources (CPR) in mitigating wealth inequality during the seventeenth-century demographic and fiscal shock in the Grand Duchy of Tuscany. Using a difference-in-differences strategy, we compare inequality trajectories between several localities with and without commons before and after the plague epidemic of 1629-1631 and the typhus outbreak of 1649-1650. Our results demonstrate that localities with commons experienced approximately 14% lower inequality growth in the post-shock period compared to those without commons. We interpret these findings as evidence that commons functioned as shock absorbers, primarily by generating municipal revenues that reduced reliance on regressive taxation and by constraining urban land acquisition.

detail.abstract: Around 13% of the UK workforce is self-employed, yet only about 6% of regulated mortgage sales in 2025 involved a borrower recorded as self-employed at application. The gap is widest among younger workers who assemble a living from platform work, short contracts, invoiced freelancing and part-time employment. Against 720,000 house purchase loans advanced in 2025, that participation gap is equivalent to roughly 50,400 loans a year; this paper decomposes it and estimates that between 7,600 and 22,700 loans a year, worth £1.5bn to £4.5bn of annual lending, are lost to measurement failure rather than to genuine affordability constraint, at a cost to each excluded household of the order of £30,000 over a five-year deferral. This paper argues that the shortfall is not caused by the FCA Handbook, which already contemplates multiple income streams and variable income, but by the absence of a defensible quantitative method for converting irregular, multi-source cash flow into an assessable income figure that a lender can evidence, stress, monitor and defend. We propose the Multi-Stream Income Reliability Assessment (MIRA): a seven-layer architecture that decomposes a borrower's cash inflows into distinct income streams, scores each stream for persistence, volatility, cadence, counterparty concentration and evidential quality, and combines them through a correlated forward-looking distribution to produce an Assessable Sustainable Income (ASI) defined as a lower quantile of predicted forward income rather than a historical average. ASI is then carried through a tax-aware net income calculation, an expenditure model that recognises the absence of statutory sick and holiday pay, a jointly specified interest-rate and income stress, and a liquidity buffer test. On an illustrative three-stream borrower, MIRA supports an advance of approximately £108,100 where a conventional variable-income rule supports none and a flat 25% haircut supports approximately £79,600, while making explicit that the modelled probability of a first-year income shortfall against contractual outgoings is 8.6%-a number that then drives buffer sizing, product structure and forbearance design rather than being hidden inside a haircut. We further show that the tail quantile is the wrong functional for this problem: where stream cessations are positively dependent, as they are for a worker whose streams share a sector, the quantile rises with that dependence and so lends most to the borrower whose income is least genuinely diversified, while the expected shortfall below it moves in the correct direction. The framework is positioned against what the market now does, including bank-derived income verification in the UK, forward-looking income forecasting shipped by data vendors in 2026, and the Dutch perspectiefverklaring, which has treated forward-looking income for flexible workers as a market standard since 2017. The paper maps every component to MCOB 11.6, to the four Consumer Duty outcomes, and to the five principles of PRA SS1/23, and sets out the validation, fairness-testing, explainability and outcome-monitoring apparatus required before such a model may responsibly be placed into production.

detail.abstract: Research on leadership has long focused on two extremes, either on individual traits (or styles and behaviors) or on relationships and context. We argue that neither extreme explains where leadership originates from or how it produces the collective outcomes it is credited with. We propose a third view that is neither a compromise between nor a variant of these extremes. We argue that leaders are theorists. Leaders are forward-looking actors who, at any level of an organization, formulate causal theories and frame problems. The value of leader theories is realized, amplified or constrained through social mechanisms. Theorizing is not one activity among many—it is the act that constitutes leading itself. The very factors foregrounded by recent work in leadership (like context, trust, and relationality) are not the starting point of leadership but emerge as leaders advocate, adopt, test, and scale theories. The leader-astheorist agenda is normative and interventionist, highlighting how leader theorizing and causal reasoning can be improved and taught. We close by laying out a research agenda for studying leaders as theorists.

detail.abstract: The practice of greenwashing has gained significance given the debate about ESG disclosures on both sides of the Atlantic. While the SEC in the US is no longer pursuing climate-related disclosure rules, the European Union has put forward an ambitious agenda, including the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD). Regardless of whether disclosures are voluntary or mandatory, there is an enforcement gap resulting from limitations on private litigation and only limited effects of reputational sanctions. This article argues that greenwashing may also have social benefits relative to the absence of sustainability disclosures. Second, social responsibility communication will attract human capital aligned with green and social goals to firms, thus gradually changing corporations from within. Third, greenwashing scandals trigger social attention that reinforces pledges and pushes the quality and quantity of greening activities throughout the economy.

detail.abstract:
Every organization operating in healthcare is running on a single, unexamined assumption, and nobody has ever gone back to check whether it actually holds. The assumption is this: that the data coming back from a state medical board, the entity standing between a physician and the first day they are legally allowed to see a patient, is itself current, accurate, and delivered on a schedule anyone can trust. Every credentialing vendor's marketing claim depends on it. Every internal thirty day target depends on it. This report is what happens when that assumption is finally treated as a hypothesis instead of a fact, and tested directly against the boards' own paper trail, their budget filings, their staffing reports, their own recorded meeting minutes. It does not hold.

The Medical Board of California, the licensing authority for the largest physician population in the country, told its own legislature, in writing, that its staff vacancy rate reached 17.37 percent in 2024, and separately disclosed borrowing ten million dollars in one fiscal year, then eight million, then six million more across the two years after, simply to keep the lights on. Texas's own legislative budget request asks for thirty and one half additional staff positions while simultaneously line itemizing money for physical document scanning, a detail that says more about the actual state of its operation than any press release ever could. Georgia's reference verification system quietly routes every professional reference straight into a general inbox, with no confirmation sent back to the applicant, a design that licensing services report produces the identical complaint over and over, a missing reference that was never actually missing. Connecticut's own licensing partners describe the entire process breaking down at the most human point possible: nobody picks up the phone.

California, Texas, Georgia, and Connecticut are not isolated failures. They are the visible edge of a pattern this report tracks across forty six states, with particular depth on New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Florida, and Texas, the exact corridor where organizational expansion and institutional fragility collide hardest. The pattern holds with uncomfortable consistency: credentialing speed correlates far more closely with a board's own staffing, its funding structure, and its institutional design than with any technology an applicant, an employer, or a vendor can ever touch. The inverse holds just as cleanly, and it is the one fact that should unsettle every board that has not fixed itself yet. Illinois cut its own average processing time from seven and one half weeks to five and seven tenths weeks in a single year, the moment direct legislative and administrative pressure landed on one specific function. The bottleneck was never unfixable. It was simply never audited, by anyone, until now.

detail.abstract: We examine whether the accounting treatment of research and development (R&D) costs affects how much effort managers devote to R&D and investors' expectations of that effort. In an incentivized laboratory market, we hold R&D costs fixed, while managers choose how to divide their unobservable effort between a routine operating project that generates certain, immediate returns and an uncertain R&D project for which additional effort increases the probability of success. We manipulate whether R&D costs are expensed or capitalized, with capitalized R&D subject to impairment testing, and whether managers are compensated based on investor-assessed market value or realized intrinsic value. We find that capitalization increases managers' R&D effort, but only when their compensation is based on investor-assessed market value, consistent with managers strategically responding to the reporting consequences of their effort choices. Investors, however, expect less managerial R&D effort under capitalization than expensing. This divergence creates systematic estimation errors, with investors overestimating R&D effort under expensing and underestimating it under capitalization. Overall, our findings show that R&D accounting interacts with managerial incentives to shape the effort managers devote to making R&D investments productive, while simultaneously biasing investors' expectations of that effort.

detail.abstract: In the newsvendor problem with quadratic rather than linear shortage and excess penalties, the optimum satises a critical ratio in which the distribution function is replaced by the normalised integrated distribution function. The solution is an expectile, and its comparison with the classical fractile solution built from the same distribution and the same cost ratio is known in the statistics literature: the two cross exactly once as the cost ratio varies, and the crossing level lies above or below one half according as the mean exceeds or falls short of the median. We give a self-contained treatment aimed at inventory and pricing applications. Four things are added. First, a proof of single crossing through two reliability functionals, which locates the crossing exactly where the mean residual life equals the mean inactivity time and reduces the sucient condition to log-concavity of a single density. Second, an exact identication: the crossing point is the unique zero of the GroeneveldMeeden skewness functional taken about x rather than about the median, so that the sign rule is literally a statement about their coecient b 3 = (µ-ν)/E|R-ν|. Third, a rst-order formula for the crossing fractile, q c-1 2 ≈ (µ-ν)f (ν)/[1-2f (ν)E|R-µ|], which identies the three functionals that govern it and contains no third moment. Fourth, a separating example: within the Weibull family the moment skewness and b 3 change sign at dierent shape parameters both are legitimate skewness measures in van Zwet's ordering and in the intervening window the crossing fractile follows b 3. Reporting the crossing fractile against a moment skewness is therefore misleading, and b 3 is the index to use.

detail.abstract: This article reexamines the common ownership theory ten years after Professor Einer Elhauge first argued that it was a violation of Section 1 of the Sherman Act and Section 7 of the Clayton Act for mutual funds and other investment vehicles to hold stock (albeit on behalf of individual investors) in competing entities.  We conclude that common ownership remains a solution in search of a problem.  Empirically, we find Elhauge and other proponents are still no closer to establishing a causal relationship between common ownership and an effect on competition than they were back in 2016.  The economic literature is at best mixed, and far from the quantum of proof policymakers and courts are likely to require.  The legal case is at least equally deficient, created out of whole cloth from the dicta of various older precedents dealing with the quite different situation of cross-ownership.  We expect some of these shortcomings to come into sharper focus as the theory is litigated, including in the Texas v. detail.abstract: Leadership and management are frequently treated as competing approaches to organizational effectiveness, yet the practical challenge for leaders is rarely choosing one over the other. Effective leadership requires recognizing what a situation demands and applying the appropriate combination of direction, coordination, adaptation, accountability, and influence. This white paper examines the leadership-management relationship through historical theory, contemporary scholarship, and practical application. It argues that leadership and management are distinct but complementary organizational capabilities and that effectiveness depends on knowing when each is required. The analysis develops a practical decision framework for assessing situational demands across organizational stability, change, complexity, people, performance, and accountability. Rather than treating leadership and management as competing identities, the paper presents them as capabilities that should be deliberately integrated. Effective organizational leadership therefore depends not only on possessing leadership and management capabilities, but on developing the judgment necessary to recognize when to lead, when to manage, and when to integrate both.

detail.abstract: Decentralized prediction markets now operate as financial infrastructure, yet they rest on the contested premise that prices efficiently aggregate dispersed information. This paper tests that premise by anchoring economic anomaly detection to legal ground truth. Purely statistical detection cannot separate an insider from a trader who processes public information unusually well, because the microstructural footprint of the two may be identical; criminal indictments, CFTC enforcement actions and documented case studies resolve that ambiguity by supplying verified positive labels. Anchored to the adverseselection frameworks of Kyle (1985) and Glosten and Milgrom (1985), a positive-unlabeled, weakly supervised Random Forest classifier is trained on four pre-resolution structural features-average entry price, capital deployed, trade count and market volume share-and applied to 889,569 trades across 93 geopolitical and military markets on Polymarket, against a descriptive baseline drawn from over 20 million deduplicated trades in 28,767 resolved markets. Leave-one-wallet-out cross-validation yields a mean AUC-ROC of 0.946. In the most informative fold, a model trained without any exposure to the wallet of a charged United States Army Special Forces servicemember ranks all four of his walletmarket observations above all eighty contemporaneous non-insider observations, placing him in the top three per cent of wallets by predicted probability. Confirmed insiders pay a median entry price of 46 cents per outcome token where comparable traders pay 77. Applied to 254,528 wallet-market pairs, the classifier returns a ranked set of unconfirmed candidates concentrated in markets where the relevant information is restricted by law. The findings suggest that prediction market accuracy and market integrity are separable, and often competing, objectives.

detail.abstract: Food exemptions permit agricultural trade under sanctions, but shipment continuity alone provides an incomplete account of supply resilience. detail.abstract: The real world operates as a complex, dynamic, nonlinear, and self-evolving ecosystem rather than a linear, mechanical, and deterministic standardized model. detail.abstract:
As AIs become progressively more capable, what does creativity mean in proposition dominant fields, like mathematics, statistics, the hard sciences and much of economics? The first claim of this essay is that the part of the debate that asks who generated the words on the page is the least interesting, least important and least useful one to have, and that the questions worth asking are upstream of examining the surface structure of the finished artifact. Moreover, the answers to these questions cannot be read off of it. I begin with the case of an AI re-rendered version of Albert Einstein's 1905 relativity paper, with the physics and his thought experiments left entirely unchanged. Run through a detector it comes back as machine-written, which, of course, it was. Yet, the intellectual content remains Einstein's alone. After coming up with an operational definition for a proposition dominant field, I conclude that conflating sentence provenance with intellectual provenance is a category error for these fields. And, I show its institutional consequences are already being felt.

Part I runs the Einstein experiment and defines the class at issue. To do this it looks at three levels, at the individual passage level, at the paper level and the field level. I introduce the idea of admissible transformation to do this. A rendering of a passage is admissible when a competent practitioner in the field would regard the transformed passage as asserting the same claims as the original. A paper is proposition dominant when such a practitioner would regard an admissibly transformed version of the whole paper as making the same contribution. Whether a field is proposition dominant is then a gray area depending on what proportion of its papers are. Part I also follows a recent case in which a detector score obliged a scholar to answer for her sentences alongside her argument, observes that many fields have long known how to separate the provenance of sentences from the provenance of ideas provided the intermediary is an expensive human editor, and ends by establishing the negative: the finished artifact alone cannot reveal its own lineage. That negative is conceded by the instruments themselves. The leading detector's published training scheme builds its labels by comparing a human source against an edited version of it, and marks a clause that carries the same claim in different words, which is to say an admissible transformation, as its middle category. It then trains a classifier to recover that label from the edited version alone, because at test time the source is not there to be had.

Part II asks what the technology is making cheap and what it leaves expensive and scarce. For example, screening a conjecture and asking a question one was once embarrassed to ask were both expensive, and are no longer, so the scholars who generate conjectures and ask foundational questions have gained ground against more cautious ones. What has not become cheaper is the idea now cast as a specification: knowing what an argument must prove before anything is generated.

Part III proposes some remedies to the scientific integrity issues that will obviously arise. My main proposal is a prompt logbook. This will be a curated, contemporaneous record of generative interactions, supported by independent timestamps and verifiable commitments. It will allow one to quantify, roughly, the level of machine involvement, but more importantly it will make a claim of intellectual provenance auditable. Part III then argues that such a record can never speak first, since a classifier costs a minute and arrives before anything else can. It closes by arguing that curating will have to be taught, for the same reason that a reading knowledge of German and, later, TeX were once taught (and required) for aspiring scholars.

A (speculative) technical coda asks what would be required to make specification a measurable quantity, using algorithmic information theory and algorithmic statistics. It states the conditions such a measure would have to satisfy and reports why some of the natural candidates fail to meet them.

detail.abstract: This study investigates how the convergence of quantum systems and artificial intelligence shapes scientific and technological evolution. It explains the growth of emerging technological domains through concepts from the economics of innovation, focusing on technological complementarities, knowledge recombination, increasing returns, and co-evolutionary dynamics. Design/Methodology/Approach Evolutionary growth models are applied to publication and patent trajectories in quantum systems, artificial intelligence, and their combined domain. Comparative relative growth rates are used to assess whether crossdomain interaction produces synergistic effects beyond the independent development of the two fields. Findings The integrated AI-quantum domain exhibits a relative growth rate of 1.58, exceeding those of quantum systems, at 1.07, and artificial intelligence, at 1.37. This result suggests that technological convergence generates superadditive effects through complementary knowledge bases and combinatorial innovation. Artificial intelligence operates as a general-purpose technology by expanding the technological opportunity set, reducing search and experimentation costs, and supporting the diffusion and commercialization of quantum applications. Quantum advances may, in turn, extend the computational frontier of artificial intelligence. Their interaction consequently creates positive feedback, knowledge spillovers, increasing returns to innovation, and pathdependent development. The asymmetric growth rates also indicate that one enabling technology can act as the principal catalyst within a mutually reinforcing innovation process. Research Limitations/Implications Publication and patent indicators may not capture tacit knowledge, informal collaboration, unsuccessful experimentation, or innovation that has not yet been codified. Future research should examine whether similar economic mechanisms characterize other technological combinations. Practical and Policy Implications Innovation policies should support interdisciplinary research, knowledge diffusion, complementary investments, shared infrastructures, and collaborative innovation ecosystems. Public and private resource allocation should target technological interfaces where interaction can produce the greatest social and economic returns. Originality/Value The study reframes AI-quantum convergence as an economic process driven by complementarities, spillovers, increasing returns, and technological interdependence.

detail.abstract: A growing class of open standards for distributed system management defines rich information models for intent-structured declarations of desired system state specifying objectives, constraints, targets, and fulfilment conditions. detail.abstract:
American corporate governance has traditionally relied on what anthropologists call a guilt-culture model of social ordering: a system in which conduct is regulated through codified prohibitions and an adjudicating authority that assesses compliance and imposes sanctions only after a formally defined rule has been broken. Corporate governance scholarship has increasingly documented that this guilt-based architecture no longer operates alone: a substantial and growing literature shows that values, environmental, social, political, and otherwise, now shape corporate behavior in ways that formal law does not fully capture, from shareholder-welfare accounts to stakeholderism to Total Governance. That literature, however, lacks a theoretical account of why values have become so consequential to corporate conduct and how, precisely, they discipline that conduct outside law’s guilt-based mechanisms.

Existing scholarship on corporate “publicness” and reputation describes exposure, showing that corporations are visible to an unprecedented degree, but exposure alone does not explain what fills the gap once a corporation’s conduct becomes visible, nor does it supply a vocabulary for describing how anticipated public judgment operates on institutions with the specificity that comparable accounts of honor and shame have long supplied for individuals. This Article identifies that theoretical gap and fills it by conceptualizing a paradigm shift from a pure guilt-culture model of corporate law to a guilt-shame model, in which a second system of social ordering, shame-culture, supplements guilt-culture’s prohibition-based accountability with a continuously operating system of public opinion.

Shame-culture, as this Article develops the concept, is a distinct paradigm of social ordering, rooted not in prohibitions and self-assessment but in aspirational models of conduct and in the assessment of the community: individuals, and by extension institutions, are held to account not by an adjudicating authority applying a codified rule, but by the perception of the public that observes them. Drawing on anthropological and classical accounts of shame-culture, the Article recovers a vocabulary, developed originally to describe honor and social ordering in Homeric and classical Greece and in Tokugawa-era Japan, capable of explaining how anticipated public judgment can regulate conduct with a granularity that existing accounts of corporate reputation and publicness do not supply. It then reconstructs the modern mechanics of public judgment by distinguishing three vectors through which the public evaluates institutions: popularity, reputation, and prestige.

Applying this framework to the modern large public company, the Article argues that popularity, reputation, and prestige now function as the specific channels through which a “court of public opinion” renders shame-based verdicts on corporate conduct, verdicts that activism translates into material pressure and that values primacy converts into durable governance commitments. The resulting guilt-shame model identifies the informal, public-opinion-driven system that operates alongside corporate law’s formal architecture, filling accountability gaps that the traditional guilt-culture model law addresses too slowly or not at all. In doing so, the Article offers corporate law scholarship its first sustained theoretical account of the mechanism, rather than merely the fact, by which values-driven public judgment governs the modern public corporation.

detail.abstract: A common development view holds that rapid growth begins with exports and later shifts to domestic demand. detail.abstract: The emission inventories of atmospheric pollutants are a diagnostic tool that offer a technical basis for developing policies and mitigation strategies. Understanding the patterns and characteristics of emissions in each study area is essential to addressing the problem. This is the first regional assessment of emission inventories of 9 major South American Metropolitan Regions (Medellín, Bogotá, Quito, Lima, Santiago de Chile, Belo Horizonte, São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Vitória). Dataset includes the information of 66 official reports published between 2000 and 2025. The information was compiled and ordered into standardized categories of emission sources (Mobile, Industrial, Resuspension, Residential and Commercial, Fires, Evaporative, Biogenic and Other) that allowed an analysis of the trends and current status of key pollutants (PM10, PM2.5, NOX, SOX, CO, VOCs among others). The results reveal significant variations in the methodologies to evaluate the emissions, pollutants analyzed, and presentation of the data. Mobile and industrial sources are responsible for most of the emissions from key pollutants. Pollutant emissions are present in different forms in the regions studied, highlighting the importance of local contexts. Although there is a growing interest in the study of the atmospheric pollution in South America through emission inventories, there is still a need for improving data quality. This unique work represents a starting point for regional efforts to standardize emission estimation methodologies, strengthen models, and promote regional plans to improve air quality and environmental health in South America.

detail.abstract:
This article distinguishes the rate of economic expansion from the durability of development. It argues that sustained growth has two immediate foundations: domestic saving determines the scale of accumulation, while productivity determines whether accumulated capital can continue to generate value after protection, exceptional prices, unused capacity, or extraordinary state demand recede. Productivity depends on science, skills, and institutions, but none is sufficient without access to a broad and technologically demanding middle class. That demand may be domestic or reached through exports of domestic value added, historically above all to the United States and Western Europe.

A modern cohort panel using OECD Trade in Value Added, World Bank, and Penn World Table data provides the empirical benchmark. Among developing industrial economies with meaningful access to qualifying demand, the interaction between saving and access predicts manufacturing value added, total factor productivity, and output per unit of capital more clearly than aggregate GDP per capita.

Historical comparisons since 1960 apply a common durability test. South Korea demonstrates how high saving, coordinated capability formation, and export discipline can convert a poor and initially narrow market into sustained technological convergence. China illustrates a similar transformation on a larger scale and the later risk of declining returns to administratively directed investment. Brazil combines genuine resource productivity with deindustrialization risk, while Mexico combines exceptional access to United States demand with insufficient saving and weak domestic diffusion. East Germany and the Soviet and Russian sequence illustrate protected, resource-dependent, and state-directed expansion. Madagascar, Niger, and Burundi show the lower boundary created by simultaneously weak accumulation and market access.

Growth is spurious not when its output is fictitious, but to the extent that its supporting mechanism cannot reproduce comparable civilian prosperity under ordinary conditions.

detail.abstract: Residential regression models commonly estimate the relationship between sale price and property characteristics available in structured data. Those data may omit or poorly represent characteristics that buyers consider important. When an omitted characteristic is correlated with a characteristic that is included in the model, part of its price influence may be reflected in the coefficient of the included variable. This paper introduces the term Value Attribution Leakage (VAL) for that interpretive problem. VAL is not a replacement for the established concept of omitted-variable bias. It describes a practical valuation consequence: apparent value can be assigned to a measured characteristic when some of that value properly belongs to an unmeasured or inadequately measured characteristic. The paper defines VAL, provides a simple residential example, distinguishes it from residual error, and proposes a basic framework for empirical testing.

detail.abstract: Indian legislation frequently entrusts decisions about maintenance, land, possession and other civil interests to officers who also administer government. detail.abstract: EU regulation is increasingly expected to deliver climate and public-health objectives while preserving competitiveness, investment, and efficient adjustment. This paper examines whether the uniform application of harmonised EU rules delivers efficient outcomes under conditions of structural heterogeneity. It compares two EU frameworks, the Emissions Trading System (ETS) and the Tobacco Products Directive (TPD), using Poland as a high-exposure stress-test case. The analysis combines ex-post evidence on ETS exposure, forward-looking scenario modelling, and comparative assessment of alternative tobacco-regulation pathways. Under the stated scenario assumptions, the arithmetic sum of the ETS baseline and TPD3 Restrictive estimates yields a model-implied 2030 reduction of €14.8 billion in Polish GDP, 209,943 jobs, and €2.63 billion in investment. detail.abstract: When a security is removed from a list of Shariah-compliant stocks, mandates tracking that list are obliged to divest. The literature has looked for the resulting price pressure at the announcement, and has generally reported it. I find that once treated firms are matched to size-comparable controls, the announcement effect disappears, whilst a substantial effect emerges months later, and that whether it emerges at all depends upon a detail of the rules which has not previously been examined, being whether the regulator grants a disposal grace period. Three samples are constructed. Malaysian routine revisions, of which there are seventeen with 259 matched pairs, carry no grace period and show nothing at any horizon. Indonesian revisions, of which there are nineteen with 123 matched pairs, likewise carry no grace period and are likewise flat. The Malaysian methodology change of November 2013, which granted a six month disposal window, underperforms its matched controls by 1.88% over twenty trading days and 5.57% over a hundred and twenty, and the gap against routine removals reaches 10.14 percentage points by day 120, t = -2.21. Two independent no-grace samples therefore behave alike whilst the single grace-period sample diverges, which is the pattern the deferred selling explanation predicts and which it could have failed. detail.abstract: The growing dependence on weather-driven variable renewable energy (VRE) sources introduces significant challenges for long-term energy system planning due to intra and inter-annual variability. Conventional approaches often rely on a single representative weather year, which can bias estimates of resource availability, demand, and optimal investments. This study introduces a framework that integrates scaled weather-dependent time series data into capacity expansion planning, where the scaling preserves the long-term distributions of multi-decadal weather variability while remaining computationally tractable. The approach is embedded in a two-stage modelling framework, where baseline investments are first optimized using the scaled time series, and system adequacy is subsequently evaluated across 39 historical weather years, with additional investments allowed under extreme weather years to ensure adequacy. The framework is applied to a pan-European, sector-coupled energy system for 2050. Results show that single weather-year based planning introduces substantial biases in weather-dependent resource availability and demand, which are mitigated through the proposed scaling approach. However, incorporating long-term distributions alone is not sufficient to ensure adequacy, as the resulting baseline system remains vulnerable under extreme weather conditions. While investment strategies based solely on extreme weather years can address adequacy concerns, the proposed two-stage approach achieves comparable adequacy by reinforcing the baseline system with targeted additional investments. We claim that VRE investment frameworks based on multi-decadal weather data better reflect developer decision-making than approaches relying on single weather years. These methodological differences lead to divergent capacity portfolios, including varying levels of dependence on storage and transmission infrastructure. Our results emphasize the importance of jointly accounting for long-term weather conditions and extreme events in energy system planning.

Overall, the results showed that the type of biomass, pyrolysis conditions and activating agent have an important effect on the yield and surface properties of the prepared biochar and activated carbon.

detail.abstract: Background: Since 2024, Google's AI Overviews and large language models have reshaped organic search, disproportionately affecting information-oriented health websites. Whether this loss of traffic translates into a loss of clinical activity is untested. Methods: Retrospective observational single-case study of a private multi-specialty practice in northern Italy with an entirely organic communication model, over 1 January 2018-31 July 2026. Traffic and activity were compared through correlation over 43 matched months, lag and Granger analysis, multivariate regression and matched 18-month windows. Results: The flagship property fell from 403,799 active users in 2024 to 172,228 annualized in 2026; the ecosystem contracted by 22.0% and then 14.0%. detail.abstract: Islamic equity screening standards diverge in a detail that is customarily treated as a technicality, being the denominator of the leverage ratio. AAOIFI divides interest-bearing debt by spot market capitalisation, whilst Dow Jones Islamic Market and S&P Shariah divide by a twenty-four month and thirty-six month trailing average respectively, and MSCI divides by total assets. Because price enters the AAOIFI denominator directly, a fall in a firm's share price mechanically raises its measured leverage and can carry it from compliant to non-compliant with no change whatsoever in the underlying business. Khatkhatay and Nisar (2007) described this mechanism in prose, however its contribution to observed compliance turnover has not to my knowledge been isolated. Garnering from SEC XBRL filings, I construct a point-in-time compliance panel for 426 US firms over 2010 to 2026, comprising 23,248 firm-quarters, and decompose every compliance transition into the portion attributable to the price move and the portion attributable to changes in reported debt. Under the AAOIFI screen, 56.9% of compliance flips are attributable to the price move alone, against 23.3% attributable to changes in debt. Substituting a twenty-four month averaged denominator, holding the screen otherwise constant, reduces the total quarterly flip rate from 5.25% to 3.22% and reduces the count of price-driven flips by 67%. Compliance churn concentrates sharply in market drawdowns, peaking in the first quarter of 2020 at roughly double the sample baseline. I believe these results carry an uncomfortable implication for the industry, in that a material share of the turnover borne by Shariah-compliant mandates is an artefact of the screening methodology rather than a response to firm conduct, and further that the choice of denominator window is a first-order design decision rather than the technical footnote it is usually taken to be.

detail.abstract: The rapid integration of Embodied Artificial Intelligence (AI) and General-Purpose AI (GPAI) into the workplace is fundamentally disrupting the traditional employer-employee dichotomy. As AI evolves from a passive technological tool into an autonomous third element capable of exercising managerial control, executives and policymakers face unprecedented legal and operational challenges. This paper explores the future of human-centric AI through a four-pillar framework: (i) the emergence of AI as a third element in labor relations; (ii) the shift toward an AI for Good paradigm that treats technology as a reasonable accommodation rather than a mere commodity; (iii) the profound liability paradoxes triggered by algorithmic opacity under the new EU frameworks (PLD and AI Act); and (iv) the urgent need to redesign EU social insurance mechanisms and workers' compensation. detail.abstract: On 28 February 2023 a head-on train collision at Tempi, Greece, killed 57 people. Systemic failures in railway modernisation were acknowledged within days, and national elections followed twelve weeks later. Linking every polling station in six contests between 2015 and 2024 to its municipal unit, I relate changes in party shares and turnout across 1,031 units to victims per 10,000 registered voters. The design is observational: victims' home units have larger electorates, lower primary-sector shares and higher incomes, lie closer to the railway, and had swung towards the incumbent New Democracy (ND) more than comparable units between 2015 and 2019. Conditional on district or municipality fixed effects and baseline levels, ND's vote share fell by 0.6 percentage points per unit of exposure in May 2023 (wildbootstrap and stratified permutation p = 0.03), ND votes per registered voter by 0.5 points, and turnout by 0.3 to 0.6 points. Between the May and June rounds exposed units moved differently from the rest of the country, with ND recovering part of its loss and the new party Niki gaining. Adjusted for the three headline hypotheses, no estimate is significant at the 5 percent level, and the intensity association is carried by six small communities; units near the railway that lost no residents show no differential response. The evidence supports a local, short-lived association between bereavement and withdrawal from the incumbent, not a national verdict on state negligence.

detail.abstract: A collective voting block can leave a development bank's host unable to protect its headquarters. Headquarters moves and prolonged transfers of operations have occurred at other multilateral banks. We examine this problem for the proposed Shanghai Cooperation Organization Development Bank. If relocation followed an illustrative weighted rule, China and Russia could approve a move over a Kyrgyz host's objection. Equal basic votes give some partners more approval opportunities while reducing those of others. Comparison with the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and New Development Bank shows how growth preserves a sponsor's block or gives founder consent an independent role. At the latter, roughly 65,700 additional entrant shares would make founder consent independently binding if founder holdings stayed fixed. These results connect the control paradox to a concrete bargain: China must value cooperation at least as much as the restraint it accepts, and the partner must receive enough protection to join. Consent to relocation and amendment of that consent offers a focused accommodation for a government seeking headquarters security.

detail.abstract: This note presents an intuitive reinterpretation of the Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) test through the lens of physical mechanics. It addresses the fundamental question of why the null hypothesis in the ADF test represents non-stationarity, even though stationarity-with constant mean, variance, and autocovariance structure-appears to describe a stable or normal state. Drawing on Newton's First Law of Motion, the discussion builds an intuitive framework where the unit root condition (H 0 : ϕ = 1) represents inertial motion without a restoring force, while stationarity (ϕ < 1) corresponds to the presence of such a force that induces mean reversion. This physical analogy transforms an abstract statistical concept into a tangible mechanism, making the ADF test's formulation logically coherent and pedagogically accessible. The approach aims to help learners in Artificial Intelligence and Time Series Forecasting understand stationarity not merely as a mathematical condition, but as a principle of dynamic equilibrium grounded in physical intuition.

detail.abstract:
We propose the category of remanent surplus value: the value transferred to each copy of a commodity by accumulated scientific knowledge-socialized in its origin, unwearable in its nature, unpaid in the present. We define remanent labor as the past labor crystallized in a support that does not wear out, and which continues to act without being consumed by its exercise. We show that this category is a second mode of labor-power in Marx's sense: an aptitude to produce, but an aptitude impermeable to use, whose cost of reproduction in the present is zero. We deduce a double accounting: value (an extensive magnitude) divides with the copies and tends toward zero; remanence (an intensive magnitude) remains whole in each copy and produces remanent surplus value. We define two production regimes by the structure of their production cycle (one-cycle vs. two-cycle regimes), propose two measurable tracers (the labor-EBIT correlation and the operating margin), and evaluate the framework on a panel of listed firms, 2015-2024, estimated by hierarchical maximum likelihood. We discuss the implications for the "techno-feudalism" debate: the super-profits of tech and pharma are proposed to be read not as rents on vassal subjects, but as the realization, copy after copy, of remanent surplus value.

detail.abstract: This study presents the development and field evaluation of an Intelligent Virtual Assistant (IVA) designed to administer structured surveys in real-world settings. The system integrates a browser-based questionnaire, visual stimuli, respondent-selected avatars, speech-to-text and text-to-speech services, and a Large Language Model decision layer that interprets spoken responses, maps them to predefined categories, and provides clarification when needed. The IVA was deployed during the housing fair (2025) in Luxembourg, where 103 participants completed an English or French survey using either voice or click-based responses. Results demonstrate that the prototype was operationally feasible and generally well received. Respondents rated the assistant positively for functionality, conversation quality, privacy, and responsiveness, although confidence in the system's ability to understand users was comparatively weaker. Voice interaction was also selective: 61% of respondents answered at least three questions orally, while 23% used voice for all items, and greater discomfort with talking to computers was associated with lower voice uptake. System logs showed that most spoken turns were processed successfully, but a substantial minority required clarification or waiting. Performance was further affected by speech-recognition errors, ambient noise, accents, question type, and response format, while French sessions generated more discarded partial speech-recognition events. The public setting may also have discouraged some respondents from answering aloud because of privacy or socialexposure concerns. The findings position IVA-administered surveys as a hybrid mode between self-administered and interviewer-led data collection. Their potential depends on mixed-modality design, robust field implementation, question-level optimization, and careful management of interaction failures and user trust.

detail.abstract: Conformal prediction has recently been proposed for the diagnosis of classifiers and the selection of federated clients, with the prediction sets themselves treated as data from which class similarity, confusion and client quality are read off. We give a specific caution in the form of a no-go theorem and a one-bit calculation. Over the class of joint laws constrained only by Ŷ ∈ C(X) whenever C(X) ̸ = ∅, the law of the prediction sets does not identify the confusion matrix once a set of size at least two occurs, and the corresponding failure inside randomized adaptive prediction sets is exhibited by construction. We illustrate with the conformal correlation matrix of Perlo et al. (2026), the phi coefficient between set membership indicators, a natural construction that is likely to be reinvented. Two classifiers built inside randomized adaptive prediction sets, exactly as Romano, Sesia and Candès specify them, produce the same matrix while confusing every class in opposite directions. Seven further hand calculations give a zero entry beside 99% directional confusion, an entry of one beside one in a million co-occurrence, and an entry of ±0.64 from pooling two clients with zero correlation on each. For classes that never share a set the entry is a function of the inclusion rates alone, and for a perfect classifier with equal top probabilities inside randomized adaptive prediction sets the matrix reveals a client's class proportions exactly, which undoes the privacy claim made for it.
